label: AHLUCONT
rationale: The Rs 890 crore Patna award is a firm award from a state government department and equals 38.5% of TTM revenue of Rs 2,312 crore (execution period not stated). The company's disclosed FY22 inflow before this award was only about Rs 229 crore, so the award is clearly larger than its disclosed history and is not routine even for an EPC business. No disqualifier shows (the company is profitable on TTM basis), and the Q1 margin and revenue jumps are low-base effects rather than the trigger.

label: AHLUCONT
rationale: The firm INR 890 cr award is 32.7% of TTM revenue of 2,723.31 cr (stated). It is not routine: it is far larger than any earlier award in the packet, even for a contractor, and the packet shows no comparable order. The INR 58.8 cr Infosys contract is small and routine. No disqualifier: the company is profitable (TTM PAT 149.94 cr) with no stress signal in the packet.

label: AWHCL
rationale: Size: the two BMC contracts total about Rs 1,330 crore over seven years, which is 137% of TTM revenue of Rs 968.97 crore on the total (about 20% per year). Firmness: both are awarded contracts from BMC, so they are firm; the subsidiary was merged into the company on 31 Dec 2025. Routine: the company wins multi-hundred-crore municipal C&T contracts regularly, so it is routine under step 3, but its market cap is 1.40x TTM revenue (below 1.5x) and TTM revenue growth is 10.2%, so the cheap-valuation exception applies and the order is decided as not routine. No disqualifier: the company is profitable with a 20.6% TTM operating margin and no losses, though its leverage and the vehicle capex to deliver the contracts are open questions.

label: AURIONPRO
rationale: The contract is stated at INR 250 cr, which is 22.9% of TTM revenue of INR 1,093 cr, and it is a received contract, so it is firm. The company calls it its largest engagement in history, which makes it non-routine, though the INR 200 cr plus Panvel order from Sep 2024 is a precedent of similar scale. No disqualifier applies, and the company is funded after its 2024 fundraise.

The 5 Aug 2026 filing states a firm order from NKG Primus JV with total size INR 400 crore, equal to 167.8% of TTM revenue of INR 238.38 crore; the period runs to March 2027 or March 2028, so annual revenue is lower than the total. Prior disclosed orders were far smaller (largest INR 94.73 crore), so the order is not routine. The awarding entity is a domestic JV, not a group entity, and no disqualifier applies; PAT was INR 29 crore in FY26 and the company is not stressed.

label: AXISCADES
rationale: The Rs 600 Cr cumulative order value is a received order from defence laboratories, equal to 58.3% of TTM revenue of Rs 1,029.96 Cr in total, or about Rs 120-200 Cr a year over three to five years (roughly 12-19% of revenue a year). It is not routine: the largest order the company has disclosed before was Rs 90 Cr (BEL, May 2024), and this award spans new airborne, naval and radar programmes. No disqualifier applies; the company is profitable (FY25 PAT Rs 75.28 Cr) and debt was largely repaid from the QIP.

label: BEML
rationale: Rs 758 crore is about 25.1% of FY20 revenue of 3,025 crore (27% of TTM). Orders were received from the MoD, so firm. The packet shows no earlier disclosure of similar orders and the size is large relative to revenue, so it is treated as not routine; the company is marginally profitable, with no disqualifier.

label: BEML
rationale: The Letter of Acceptance from BMRC for Rs 3,177 crore is a firm external award directly to BEML, equal to 83.5% of TTM revenue of Rs 3,806.68 crore (total value, tenure not stated). It is not routine: the company's recent orders were Rs 378-423 crore, and the 2021 MMRDA order is the only larger one in the packet, with no value stated. Q1 FY24 losses and the unexplained margin rise are open research questions, not disqualifiers, since the company is profitable on a trailing basis.

label: BDL
rationale: Size: USD 255M is about INR 2,091 cr at an assumed INR 82/USD, or 68.1% of TTM revenue of INR 3,072.21 cr (periods run to Dec 2022). Firm: a received export order is binding demand. Not routine: no prior export orders appear in the packet, and this is a new market for the company, even though its domestic order sizes are comparable. No disqualifier: the company is profitable with positive PBT in the latest quarters, and the counterparty is external. The main open items are the unnamed counterparty and the FX assumption.

label: BHEL
rationale: The stated value is Rs 23,000 crore over the contract life, against FY22 revenue of Rs 21,211 crore, or 108.4%; supply alone (80 x Rs 120 crore = Rs 9,600 crore) is still about 45% of that revenue, so the threshold is met either way. The consortium award is a received order from the Ministry of Railways, so it is firm. It is not routine, since it is more than twice the largest earlier award and opens passenger rolling stock. The unresolved items are BHEL's consortium share and execution funding, and the company is profitable in FY22, so it is not stressed.

label: BLUSPRING
rationale: Four firm contracts awarded to the acquired subsidiary STEAG total Rs 5,112 cr over five years, which is 151% of FY26 revenue of Rs 3,382 cr (about 30% a year on the five-year term); the STEAG base sits outside the consolidated figures. The new awards of Rs 3,487 cr are about 7.6 times the company's own full-year FY26 new contract value and add power O&M as a new vertical, so they are not routine; the Rs 1,625 cr of renewals are continuity only. No disqualifier is shown: STEAG is described as net cash, and the company's TTM loss of Rs 23 cr is small with falling debt.

label: BUTTERFLY
rationale: The 285 cr order is stated in value and is 32.8% of TTM revenue of INR 869.64 cr, and the company has received it as a binding award from a state procurement body. It is not routine: it is about 3.2x the largest prior order in the packet (90 cr Pondicherry), though earlier TNCSC awards are referenced without size, which keeps this at medium confidence. No one-off, stressed, fatal-flaw or internal-demand disqualifier is visible; execution period and whether this procurement recurs are open.

label: CEIGALL
rationale: The Letter of Award is firm and the 1,089 crore project cost is 31.5 percent of TTM revenue of 3,452.52 crore, multi-year total. The company regularly wins orders of this size, so the award is routine, but the price to sales of 1.37 is below the 1.5 cheap-valuation threshold and TTM operating margin is 14 percent, so the exception applies and it is decided as not routine. The company is profitable and has no disqualifier, though TTM revenue growth is not shown and the order book check found no company total in the listed documents.

label: CENTUM
rationale: Size: the stated INR 300 crore contract is 27.7% of TTM revenue of INR 1,083.92 crore (the packet's own figure is 27.2%; the difference is rounding or base). It is firm because management says the company has won it. It is not routine: the largest disclosed prior orders are DRDO payload orders without values or a ~INR 80 crore delivery in 2024, so this is clearly bigger and opens a satellite-payload EW line. Losses (TTM PAT -30 crore) and a pending fund raise are risks, but the debt level and the FY24 customer advances do not make it a stressed company, so no disqualifier applies.

Size is stated: the four firm purchase orders total about INR 18.52 crore against FY26 revenue of INR 55.37 crore, which is 33.4%. They are firm because they are purchase orders (the engine's NON_BINDING tag is wrong), and the 8.14 crore BHEL order is part of this total, not an addition. They are not routine: the company's prior aggregates were about INR 6 crore, and the 140-160T power-plant cranes extend the high-capacity class first won in March 2026. Even if treated as routine, the TTM operating margin of 8.2% (below 10%) and FY26 revenue growth of 7.4% (51.54 to 55.37) meet the thin-margin exception, so the outcome is unchanged; no disqualifier is visible.

label: DCXINDIA
rationale: The stated order of about US$55.13 million is INR 457.6 crore at the packet's 83/USD rate, or about 32.1% of TTM revenue of 1,423.58 crore. It is a received purchase order, so firm, and it comes from a new overseas customer, much larger than the company's other disclosed orders (for example the US$2 million Lockheed PO), so it is not routine. No disqualifier applies, and the company is profitable with the debt reduced and QIP proceeds raised, but the period of execution and production readiness are open questions for deep research. The earlier 28.3% figure was miscalculated and is replaced here.

label: DEEPINDS
rationale: Firm: a letter of award from ONGC. The stated Rs 1,402 cr is the 15-year total, which is 312.2% of TTM revenue of Rs 449 cr on the total basis, or about 20.8% a year. Not routine: it is roughly ten times the largest award disclosed in the packet (Rs 135 cr), and it opens a long-duration production-enhancement service line. No disqualifier applies; the company is debt-free.

label: DIVGIITTS
rationale: The 800 crore lifecycle contract is firm; comparing the seven-year total with TTM revenue of 236.36 crore, as the rule requires, gives 338.5% (about 48% a year). It is not routine: it is larger than any single order disclosed before (the largest single one was about 47 crore) and sits in the core transfer-case line. No disqualifier is visible, but the order was first disclosed in Aug 2024, so deep research should check prior triage status.

label: DREDGECORP
rationale: Firm award from SMPA of 2,015.88 INR crore for five years of maintenance dredging. The total is 213.2% of trailing revenue of 945.50 INR crore (about 42.6% a year). The packet shows no comparable award before, so it is not routine. The counterparty is an external government port authority and there is no stress or other disqualifier; the signed contract and annual phasing are open.

label: DSSL
rationale: The Rs 750.82 cr RBI award is 55.6% of TTM revenue of Rs 1,350.74 cr (stated) and is a received, firm order. Dynacons wins private-cloud contracts regularly, but at about three times its largest prior single award this is clearly bigger than anything disclosed, so it is not routine; the cheap-valuation exception (price to sales 1.23, TTM OPM 10.3%, TTM revenue growth +10.7%) would also allow deep research. No disqualifier applies: it is a single named award, the company is profitable and growing, and the packet shows no distress.

label: ENDURANCE
rationale: Rs 9.4 bn of booked OEM orders equals 10.7% of TTM revenue of Rs 8,804 crore (STATED), and booked orders count as firm. It is not routine: the investor presentation shows EV share of orders rising from 12% to 42% with 15 new EV programmes, a new revenue stream compared with earlier disclosures that show only small orders such as EUR 19.3 mn in FY21. The period of the Rs 9.4 bn figure is not stated, and the Rs 6 bn EV figure may overlap it, so the 10.7% uses only the Rs 9.4 bn figure. Balance sheet is not stressed (TTM PAT Rs 480 crore, low finance cost).

Firm ONGC order of 44.66 crore incl. GST, about 37.8 crore ex-GST or 59% of TTM revenue of 64.13 crore. It is not routine: it is roughly 1.7 times the prior high of about 26 crore and comes from a new customer. The company is profitable, so no stressed-company disqualifier applies, but TTM operating margin of 9.4%, falling revenue and an unresolved preferential issue are open questions for deep research.

label: GVT&D
rationale: Size: the largest listed Q4 FY24 order is INR 57,912 million (about 5,791 crore), roughly 183% of trailing revenue of 3,167.91 crore, though the period over which it executes is not stated. Firm: the orders are received orders from named customers. Not routine: the packet's earlier disclosed orders run about 370 to 800 crore, and management calls this the highest inflow in a decade, so these are clearly bigger than anything disclosed before. No disqualifier: the company is debt-free with profits in FY24, the customers are external utilities and EPCs, and the demand is not one-off.

label: GOLDIAM
rationale: The Rs 1,400 million of orders won in Q1 FY25 is stated and equals 21.6% of TTM revenue of Rs 648.90 crore, with a company-total order book of about Rs 1,500 million at 30 June 2024. It is not routine, because the largest quarterly inflow disclosed earlier was about Rs 700 million, so the quarter is roughly double the prior peak. The company is debt-free with about Rs 3,332 million of cash, so no stressed-company or other disqualifier applies.

label: HECPROJECT
rationale: A received work order (firm) from RVNL, an external state PSU, worth Rs 62.1 crore against trailing revenue of Rs 59.5 crore, so about 104% of revenue. It is bigger than any order in the packet's history (largest previous Rs 37.0 crore), so it is not routine. No disqualifier applies: the company is small but profitable, and the order is external rather than internal demand. Execution period, margin and funding are unresolved.

label: HIRECT
rationale: The order is stated as more than Rs 200 crore, about 41.9% of trailing revenue of Rs 477.78 crore (200 / 477.78). The filing is a received domestic supply order from Indian Railways with no related-party interest, so it is firm. It is not routine: the only other disclosed order in the packet is Rs 70.40 crore in 2022. No disqualifier applies; the company is profitable on a trailing basis (PAT 4.94 crore).

label: ITI
rationale: The Rs 3,889 crore BSNL APO is a received purchase order and equals 220.8% of TTM revenue of Rs 1,762 crore (total over 24 months; about 110% a year). It is not routine: it is roughly nine times the Rs 433 crore BharatNet order and opens 4G telecom, a new customer and product line. ITI has heavy quarterly losses and finance cost, which could be a stressed-company disqualifier, but an order of this size is plausibly the fix for the cost base, so the disqualifier is not applied; margin and funding are open for research.

label: JKIL
rationale: The MMRDA order is firm and stated at INR 1,998 crore, about 81.3% of TTM revenue of INR 2,456.63 crore (67% of FY20 revenue), well above the 10% line. It is not routine on the packet: it is about 30% larger than the NHAI INR 1,540 crore order in the company's own milestone slide and far above a normal 20 to 40% order, although that comparable makes the routine test contestable. Trailing PAT is positive and management calls the company almost net debt free, so there is no stress disqualifier.

label: JASH
rationale: Size: the INR 100 cr Singapore order is 33.4% of FY21 revenue of INR 299 cr; the INR 40 cr Hong Kong order adds 13.4%. Firm: the investor presentation says the orders are already secured. Not routine: earlier disclosures show only about INR 15 cr of orders, and these are a new export market and far larger. No disqualifier shown; the company is profitable (TTM PAT INR 30.5 cr) and the work is infrastructure, not one-off.

label: JBMA
rationale: 700 buses x assumed INR 60 lakh (low end for an AC CNG low-floor bus) = ~420 crore, about 27.9% of TTM revenue 1,506 crore (21.6% of FY20). The LoA from an external government customer is firm, and a single order of this size is clearly bigger than anything else in the packet, not routine flow. The company is profitable and no disqualifier applies.

label: JWL
rationale: The INR 514.60 crore order is a firm, received supply order from Indian Railways equal to 43.7% of FY22 revenue (INR 1,178.35 crore), well above the 10% threshold. The packet shows no earlier JWL order of comparable size, so it is provisionally non-routine, although the word 'additional' suggests earlier wagon orders from the same customer that the packet does not show. No disqualifier applies: the company is profitable and the demand is external. Routine status and execution timing need checking in deep research.

label: JWL
rationale: Size: the 1,617 crore LoA against TTM revenue of 2,988.61 crore is about 54.1%, and the value is stated. Firmness: the Ministry of Railways has issued a Letter of Acceptance, which is a received award. Not routine on the packet evidence: the other disclosed orders are much smaller (USD 8 million, 200 crore brake discs, 10 crore pilot), so this is clearly bigger than anything shown. No disqualifier: the external government buyer is not one-off, and the company is profitable and raised equity in the QIP, though the 51 older passages left out leave the routine test incomplete.

label: KRYSTAL
rationale: Size: Rs 275 crore total over five years is 21.2% of TTM revenue of Rs 1,295.96 crore, about 4% a year. Firm: work orders from VVCMC (a government body) are received for Rs 83 crore and Rs 111 crore, with the third contract implied. Routine by pattern: the company regularly wins contracts of this size (Rs 370 crore, Rs 349 crore, Rs 168 crore in 2025), so routine=true, but the TTM operating margin of 6.5% and market cap of 0.67x TTM revenue trigger the exception, and TTM revenue growth of +18.0% is above zero, so it is decided as non-routine. No disqualifier: the company is rated A-/Stable and the work is a first large municipal SWM award.

label: LUMAXIND
rationale: Size: INR 475 crore against TTM revenue of INR 2,261 crore is 21.0%; no execution period is stated, so the total is compared with one year. Firm: binding orders from OEMs against an INR 1,150 crore order book, not a non-binding pipeline. Not routine: the largest comparable order announcement in the packet is INR 250 crore (2021), and the orders are tied to a new facility adding capacity. No disqualifier: TTM PAT is about INR 111 crore; open items are conversion timing, customer identity and funding of the facility.

label: MANAKCOAT
rationale: A signed European contract worth about 200 INR crore is 26.3% of trailing revenue of 761.73 INR crore, with the execution period not stated. The packet shows no comparable order in the company's history, and the company itself calls it landmark and export-led, so it is not routine. The company is not stressed: debt is low, the rating was upgraded, and the preferential issue is funding growth; the open items are recurrence and execution timing.

label: MANORAMA
rationale: Commercial production has started at a new 25,000 TPA fractionation plant, which makes it firm (capacity commissioned and operating). Sized at 25,000 TPA x 50% utilisation x an assumed Rs 250/kg realisation, it is about Rs 312.5 crore, or about 68% of TTM revenue of Rs 457.08 crore, so the estimate is sensitive to the price assumption. This is a step-change in the company's fractionation line (about +167% capacity), not routine flow, and no disqualifier applies: the company is profitable and the packet shows no stress.

label: MINDACORP
rationale: Size: the 750 crore lifetime battery-charger order against TTM revenue of 4,364.41 crore is about 17.2% on the total, with the period not stated. Firmness: the company says it has secured the order from a leading OEM, so it is a received award. Not routine: the 750 crore order is larger than any single order in the packet's history (about 200-230 crore), and it adds new EV customers; the 3,000 crore headline is a quarterly aggregate and is not used. No disqualifier: the company is near net-debt free, though its PAT fell in Q1 FY24.

label: NBCC
rationale: Size: INR 1,800 cr is 26.3% of FY21 revenue of INR 6,832 cr; execution period not stated. Firm: awarded and received; the award is external (Rajasthan government) even though it goes to a subsidiary, so it is not internal demand. Not routine: about 3.8x the largest valued disclosure and about 3 months of revenue, although several smaller PMC awards appear. The company was debt-free with cash surplus per its March 2021 presentation; open questions are NBCC's share of execution and the timing.

label: NETWEB
rationale: The 1,734 crore order is stated as secured and is 133.3% of TTM revenue of 1,300.92 crore, with execution due between Q4 FY26 and H1 FY27, so it is a near-term step-change. It is not routine: the largest disclosed order before was about 147 crore, and the order opens a sovereign-AI infrastructure segment. No disqualifier is shown; deep research should check the counterparty, hardware margin and working capital.

label: NIBE
rationale: Size: the stated NIBE share of INR 563.35 crore, executed within 12 months, is 123.8% of TTM revenue of INR 454.96 crore. Firmness: a signed contract with the Indian Army, so it is firm. Not routine: it is more than 1.9x the largest previously disclosed order (INR 292.69 crore) and opens loitering munitions as a new product line. Not stressed: losses are modest against revenue and equity was raised in Mar and Jun 2026, though leverage is unknown.

label: NIRAJ
rationale: Size: the INR 220.89 crore MMRDA work order over three years (excluding GST, confirmed in the filing annexure) is 35.3% of trailing four-quarter revenue of INR 625 crore. Firmness: a work order from a domestic government authority is received, so it is firm, and the filing states no related-party interest. It is not shown to be routine: the packet gives no earlier order of this size with a value, and revenue has scaled up sharply from INR 63-160 crore a quarter in 2021-22 to INR 314 crore in March 2023. No disqualifier applies, but thin profitability and unknown working-capital needs are the main open questions.

label: OLECTRA
rationale: An external state transport undertaking firmly awarded 350 electric buses to EVEY, which will procure them from Olectra, so this is treated as Olectra's own firm pass-through order. Estimated size: 350 buses x INR 1.0 cr (low end for an e-bus) = about INR 350 cr, roughly 184% of TTM revenue of INR 190 cr, delivered over 12 months. Olectra has only L1 positions in its earlier disclosures and revenue near INR 200 cr a year, so this is clearly a step-change; related-party execution and funding are open items, not disqualifiers.

label: OMINFRAL
rationale: Letter of Award of INR 621 cr is about 378% of TTM revenue (INR 164 cr), firm, and much larger than anything else in the company's disclosures. The L1 news two weeks earlier is the same event but was not an earlier triage, and the company is profitable with modest finance cost, so no disqualifier. Execution period and funding remain open for research.

Stated order of INR 226.13 crore (USD 23.66m) against TTM revenue of INR 185.89 crore gives 121.6%, well above the 10% threshold (size STATED). The order is firm (received 2026-09-13), company-specific, and non-routine: no earlier comparable order is disclosed and it is larger than any year of reported revenue in the packet. Counterparty and execution period are unknown, ADTV is only INR 0.31 crore, and no disqualifier applies. TTM OPM is 10.0% and TTM PAT is INR 6.85 crore, so the company is not stressed.

label: POWERMECH
rationale: The Rs 6,163 crore Adani FGD order is firm and external, and it equals 217% of trailing revenue of Rs 2,834 crore; the total is well above the Rs 343 to 2,120 crore awards disclosed earlier. The company calls it a record order and it adds a new thermal FGD scope, so it is not routine even though the company wins large contracts regularly. No disqualifier applies, and the execution period is the main open question.

Size: the stated Rs 37 crore order, to be executed within FY27, is 46.8% of FY26 revenue of Rs 79.02 crore. It is firm, since the company says it has received the order from the Ministry of Home Affairs. It is not routine: the earlier orders were mostly Rs 0.5-2.7 crore, so this is roughly 14 times the largest prior order and a new central-government customer. No disqualifier is shown, although whether the order is a one-off procurement is open and the TTM operating margin of 8.4% is thin; the company reported a small profit (FY26 PAT Rs 0.61 crore).

label: PSPPROJECT
rationale: The 880 cr award is stated as received, equal to 32.5% of TTM revenue of 2,706 cr, so the size test passes. It is firm, and orders of this size recur for this company, so it is routine under the base test. The thin-margin and cheap-valuation exception applies (TTM OPM 6.0%, market cap 1.14x TTM revenue) and TTM revenue growth is +8.0%, so it is treated as non-routine and sent to deep research. No disqualifier: the company is not stressed (finance cost about 11 cr a quarter, credit limits available).

label: PTCIL
rationale: A firm order of over INR 100 crore from BrahMos Aerospace is about 28% of TTM revenue of INR 358 crore, with the execution period not stated. It is not routine: none of the company's earlier defence orders in the packet was disclosed with a value, and BrahMos is a new customer for a new casting product. The company is profitable (TTM PAT INR 61 crore) and funded, so no disqualifier applies; the main open questions are the delivery schedule and margin.

label: RAMKY
rationale: The INR 1,297 crore HMWSSB contract, awarded to a subsidiary of the company, equals 60% of TTM revenue of INR 2,161 crore (contract period not stated, so this is a total-value comparison). It is an external government award, so it is firm and counts as the company's own order under the pass-through rule. The largest prior award in the packet is about INR 107 crore, so it is non-routine and opens a build-and-operate wastewater stream. Funding and the balance sheet are not in the packet, but the company is profitable and no heavy-loss disqualifier applies, so deep research is warranted.

label: REFEX
rationale: Stated value INR 750 crore against FY25 revenue of INR 2,467.66 crore (TTM equal to FY25) is about 30.4%, to be executed in FY26. It is a received order from an external utility (Torrent Power), so firm, though the packet's record conflicts on this and the value is management-stated. It is not routine: the release calls it the first major order for wind turbine supply, a new product line for the group. Pre-existing earnings are strong (FY25 PAT INR 158 crore), and equity raised in the preferential issue, so no stress or fatal-flaw disqualifier applies.

label: RICOAUTO
rationale: Size: management's annualized INR 1,000 cr less the INR 355 cr already done leaves about INR 645 cr, which is 43.9% of FY21 revenue of INR 1,470 cr (the full 1,000 cr would be 68%). Firm: deliveries have started, so operations have commenced. Not business as usual: a repricing and exit programme plus new businesses after import curbs is a turnaround from a specific operating event. The company is loss-making on a TTM basis, but the event is the fix; funding is not verified.

label: SALASAR
rationale: The Rs 252 cr is a signed work contract (presentation page 7), not an L1 bid, so it is firm and equals about 51% of trailing revenue of Rs 493.7 cr. The packet shows no earlier comparable order and the metro ballastless-track scope is new to the disclosed segments, so not routine on the available evidence. Trailing PAT is positive at Rs 23.8 cr and debt is not shown as stressed, so no disqualifier; contract terms and the Texmaco pass-through are the main open questions.

label: SALASAR
rationale: Size: two PVVNL orders total about INR 750 crore against TTM revenue of INR 922 crore, or 81.3% in total over about 24 months (about 40% a year if spread evenly). Firm: received orders from a state utility, a company-specific binding award. Not routine: the largest order previously disclosed in the packet is about INR 252 crore, so this is about 3x any earlier award. No disqualifier; working-capital funding and margins are the open questions.

label: SANGHVIMOV
rationale: Firm work orders of Rs 150 crore (received, binding) equal 32.9% of TTM revenue of Rs 455.78 crore, which is well above the Rs 35 crore largest order previously disclosed, so this is a step-change rather than routine flow. The counterparties are external IPPs, the company is profitable with PAT of Rs 112 crore TTM, and no disqualifier applies. Execution period is not stated, so the annual revenue contribution is unknown.

label: SHAKTIPUMP
rationale: The HAREDA work order is a firm award of about Rs 358 crore, equal to 43.3% of TTM revenue of Rs 826 crore on the stated GST-inclusive value (about 37% excluding GST). It is not routine because the packet shows no earlier domestic firm award of this size: the company's domestic tenders were L1 positions, and its largest firm order was the USD 35.30 million Uganda contract. No disqualifier applies, but execution timing, payment terms and the earlier on-hold KUSUM-2 volumes are open questions for deep research.

label: SHAKTIPUMP
rationale: Size: the 600.58 crore Letter of Award (ex-GST) is 23.1% of TTM revenue of 2,602.94 crore, with no stated execution period. Firm: a received Letter of Award from a state renewable agency under PM-KUSUM. Not routine: it is about 5.6 times the largest domestic PM-KUSUM award in the packet (107.33 crore ex-GST, April 2025) and about twice the USD 35.3 million Uganda contract (January 2025), and it opens a new state customer. No disqualifier: PM-KUSUM is a recurring government programme, and the company is profitable with a 292.6 crore QIP closed in July 2025 (funding shown as FUNDED).

label: SIEMENS
rationale: The INR 26,000 crore Indian Railways award is firm (a Letter of Award was received) and is 161.1% of FY22 revenue of INR 16,137.80 crore on the multi-year total, so the annual share is lower and the period is not stated. It is not routine: the company calls it its single largest order in India and it opens an electric-locomotive product line that the packet shows no earlier comparable for. No disqualifier applies: the company is profitable (FY22 PAT about INR 1,543 crore) and the order is not one-off, internal or already in reported results.

label: SKIPPER
rationale: Size: Rs 1,429 cr Q3 FY26 order inflow = 27.6% of TTM revenue (Rs 5,174 cr). Firm: received orders, and the book roll-forward (8,820 to 9,009 cr with Q3 revenue 1,371 cr) implies about 1,560 cr of intake, consistent with that figure. Routine: quarterly inflows of Rs 1,243 to 1,900 cr are regular, so routine=true, but the cheap-valuation exception applies (market cap 4,142 cr is 0.80x TTM revenue) with TTM revenue growth of 15.2%, so decided as not routine; TTM OPM 10.8% is not thin. No disqualifier shown; funding and dilution need checking.

label: SOMICONVEY
rationale: The stated order of Rs 46.61 cr is 44.1% of TTM standalone revenue of Rs 105.62 cr (total value, execution period not stated), and it is a firm secured order. The packet has no earlier comparable order disclosures, so it is clearly larger than anything the company has disclosed and is not routine. No disqualifier is evident from the packet, though the buyer is unnamed and related-party demand has not been excluded.

label: SONATSOFTW
rationale: A USD 160 million (about INR 1,312 crore at an assumed 82 INR/USD) contract is 17.1% of TTM revenue of 7,685.79 crore, stated in the filing. The company awarded it as a contract win and calls it its largest-ever, far above anything in the packet's earlier disclosures, so it is not routine. The company is profitable with no disqualifier; the unknowns are the contract term and the FX basis, which affect the size estimate.

label: SOUTHWEST
rationale: Firm contracts from external state entities total Rs 29.64 crore (ONGC NOA Rs 18.64 cr and SAIL PO Rs 11 cr), about 25.2% of TTM revenue of Rs 117.62 crore; the Rs 7.10 crore Hutti Gold item is only an LOI and is excluded from firmness. The order is clearly bigger than the company's prior Rs 1-5 crore awards and opens geothermal drilling, a first in its history, so it is not routine. The company is profitable (TTM PAT Rs 8.72 crore) with no stress flag, and the event is company-specific with no disqualifier.

label: STLTECH
rationale: Size: the stated order value is 'exceeding Rs 500 cr' for the data-centre portfolio, 11.5% of TTM revenue of Rs 4,362 cr (a floor; execution period unknown). Firm: orders secured in Q3 FY26. Not routine: no comparable sized order appears in the packet, and data-centre supply at this scale is a step-change from the telecom and interconnect wins disclosed before. No disqualifier: TTM losses are modest (PAT -Rs 43 cr) and the Rs 1,000 cr QIP of 2024 already reduced debt, though leverage (finance cost about Rs 226 cr a year) is an open research question.

label: TECHNOE
rationale: Size is the stated INR 1,750 cr award, 141.8% of TTM revenue of INR 1,234.5 cr, though the execution period is not stated. It is firm (awarded, not L1) and company-specific, and it is not routine at this scale: the packet shows no awarded order this large before (prior flows were about INR 600 cr over nine months, and the INR 1,600 cr FGD orders were L1 positions). No disqualifier applies: the company is debt-free and profitable and the client is an external party.

label: TEXRAIL
rationale: Stated value Rs 6,450 crore over 39 months equals 397.7% of TTM revenue of Rs 1,621.74 crore; per the rule the multi-year total is compared with annual revenue. The order is firm (bagged from a railway tender) and no comparable order appears in the packet's history, so it is not routine. No disqualifier: TTM PAT is positive at Rs 20.53 crore and the customer is an external state railway; the 39-month phasing and funding remain open for deep research.

label: TARIL
rationale: Received order of INR 235 crore from GETCO against TTM revenue of 936.34 crore: 25.1%. Firm (received order) and from an external state utility. Not routine: the largest prior disclosed order was 108 crore and no disqualifier is shown; the equity raise in the lookback and the unstated execution period are open questions for research.

label: TRITURBINE
rationale: The INR 1.0 billion SADC servicing order is a received contract equal to about 10.8% of trailing revenue of INR 927 crore, so it passes the 10% size test as stated, though the execution period is not given. The company calls it a new aftermarket stream for utility turbines, outside its conventional business, and the packet shows no comparable services order, so it is not routine. It is a maintenance contract with lower margins, and the packet gives no mechanism for margin change, so the margin effect is open.

The Letter of Award worth Rs 40.25 crore is 44.2% of TTM revenue of Rs 91.13 crore, with no execution period stated, and an LoA counts as a firm award. Orders of this size are rare in the packet: the Rs 41.35 crore January 2025 order was the company's largest to date, and the March 2025 GETCO letter of intent was similar, so this is not a routine monthly order. No disqualifier applies: TTM PAT is Rs 25.28 crore, TTM operating margin is 38.6%, and finance cost is negligible.

label: WELCORP
rationale: The Anjar TMT plant has started dispatches, so the event is firm (commercial shipment) and company-specific. Size is estimated at about 13.4% of FY2022 revenue from 350 KMT capacity at 50% year-one utilisation and an assumed Rs 50,000/t, since the Rs 665 cr figure is backlog and not sizable revenue. It is not routine because TMT bars are a new steel product line, and no disqualifier applies, though the Dec 2022 quarter overlap and funding remain open.

label: WELENT
rationale: A received Letter of Acceptance from BMC, directly to Welspun Enterprises, is firm. Total contract value Rs 4,123.88 crore is 142.4% of trailing revenue of Rs 2,896.25 crore; the packet gives no annual split, so the 48-month plus 15-year period is noted in missing_information. It is not routine: the largest comparable in the packet is a 2021 JV of about Rs 2,500 crore, and this adds a municipal DBO with an O&M annuity. No disqualifier applies; the company is profitable on a trailing basis.
